page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance managed by the Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor from the ARMv9 family, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V3 model. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache architecture consists of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core testing, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing. Passmark memory testing also ranks in the top tier. However, multi-core and complex computational tests generally fall into the average category, including Geekbench multi-core, stress-ng multi-core, and static web serving throughput. Weaknesses are observed in Passmark CPU encryption and medium-sized LLM inference prompt processing, where the 7B model achieved a poor rating.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver high single-threaded efficiency and memory performance relative to its resource footprint. The lack of hyperthreading ensures dedicated execution resources per vCPU, though the absence of local NVMe storage requires external block storage for persistent data. This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, lightweight web serving, and database operations that benefit from high memory bandwidth and strong single-core execution.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by a 3.3 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing 16.0 GB of system memory. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core execution, memory speed, and single-threaded compression, though multi-core operations and cryptographic tasks fall into average or weak categories. Qualitatively, the dedicated core architecture offers predictable performance per resource unit. This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, including text processing, database operations, and lightweight web serving.
